title: Did you know that mashing up two games has always been allowed?
author: clerveu
selftext:
It's totally free and legal! Well... free at any rate! j/k *obviously* anyone who does this will only be using their own ROMs. 

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=16FlEcalyIg

I can't express how much childhood traumua Claude helped me resolve in the space of about 2 hours this weekend. This was accomplished in just a handful of prompts. I'm not entirely sure but I *think* Claude ended up decompiling the entirety of Contra III all by itself. I can't wait to see the "remixes" people are going to come up with using this technique, it doesn't even need to be limited to two games. 

Apologies if this trend already came and went here but I'm seeing it all over everywhere else (mostly with modern games) but haven't really seen it talked about here much. 

I went ahead and put a repo together you can point your agent at to save a little bit of time, but as it was Claude didn't really seem to need to do a ton of work to know how to do this, so honestly just saying "Hey, I heard people were doing this, let's try" might be sufficient. 

https://github.com/Clerveu/snesmash-kit

comments.author: Valdaraak
comments.body:
Just general venting, not really directed at you personally:

Man, these "I put X game into Y game" posts are getting about as annoying as all the "X game recompiled to work natively on PC" videos and repos.

replies.author: clerveu
replies.body: Okay, that's always been allowed too!
